content.user_title: Implement SLO Monitoring and Error Budgets
content.value_statement: Teams struggle to set reliability targets that connect telemetry to delivery decisions. This skill guides SLO design, SLIs, error budgets, dashboards, alerts, and review practices.
actual_capabilities: Defines SLO frameworks for service tiers, user journeys, and business impact.
Selects practical SLIs for availability, latency, error rate, and user outcomes.
Calculates error budgets and explains how to use them in release decisions.
Designs monitoring, dashboards, and burn-rate alerts for SLO tracking.
Provides reporting and governance templates for recurring SLO reviews.
limitations: Requires accurate service telemetry before targets can be validated.
Cannot confirm production readiness without access to real metrics and incidents.
Provides implementation guidance, not managed monitoring infrastructure.
Example thresholds must be adapted to each service and stakeholder expectation.

use_cases.title: Launch a New SLO Program
use_cases.description: Create initial service tiers, SLIs, targets, and review routines for teams that lack reliability standards.

use_cases.title: Improve Alert Quality
use_cases.description: Replace noisy threshold alerts with burn-rate alerts tied to user impact and error budget consumption.

use_cases.title: Connect Reliability to Roadmaps
use_cases.description: Use error budget status to guide release pacing, reliability work, and stakeholder conversations.

prompt_templates.title: Define Basic SLOs
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define initial SLOs for a service. Ask for the service purpose, users, current telemetry, incidents, and business impact before proposing targets.

prompt_templates.title: Select SLIs From Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these available metrics and recommend SLIs for availability, latency, and correctness. Explain which metrics are weak proxies and which need validation.

prompt_templates.title: Design Burn-Rate Alerts
prompt_templates.prompt: Design multi-window burn-rate alerts for my SLOs. Include alert intent, severity, paging criteria, and steps to verify that alerts reflect user impact.

prompt_templates.title: Build an SLO Governance Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an SLO governance plan for multiple teams. Include service tiers, review cadence, error budget policy, reporting format, and rollout milestones.

output_examples.input: Create an SLO plan for a checkout API with payment dependency risk.
output: Recommended SLIs: successful checkout completion, request availability, p95 latency, and payment dependency failure rate.
Suggested targets: 99.9% checkout success and p95 latency under 500 ms, pending baseline validation.
Next steps: confirm stakeholder expectations, collect four weeks of data, and add burn-rate alerts.

output_examples.input: Our team has too many latency alerts. Improve the alert strategy.
output: Keep paging alerts tied to fast error budget burn and user-facing latency SLO breaches.
Move trend-only latency changes to tickets or dashboards unless they threaten the error budget.
Review alert history monthly to remove alerts that do not lead to action.

output_examples.input: Prepare a monthly SLO review for an authentication service.
output: Summarize target versus actual availability, latency, and error budget remaining.
List incidents that consumed budget and assign follow-up owners.
Recommend whether the next month should prioritize reliability work or feature delivery.

best_practices: Start with user journeys and business impact before choosing metrics or targets.
Validate SLO targets against historical telemetry before using them for decisions.
Tie paging alerts to error budget burn and clear operator action.
anti_patterns: Do not set aspirational targets without baseline data or stakeholder agreement.
Do not alert on every SLI movement when no immediate action is expected.
Do not use sensitive or personal data directly in monitoring labels, dashboards, or alerts.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide service purpose, user journeys, available metrics, recent incidents, dependency risks, and stakeholder expectations.

faq.question: Can this skill choose SLO targets automatically?
faq.answer: It can recommend targets, but final targets should be validated against telemetry and business expectations.

faq.question: Does it create monitoring infrastructure?
faq.answer: It provides designs, examples, and implementation guidance. You still need to apply changes in your monitoring stack.

faq.question: Which monitoring tools does it support?
faq.answer: The playbook includes Prometheus, Grafana, alerting, reporting, and general observability patterns that can be adapted.

faq.question: How does it reduce noisy alerts?
faq.answer: It favors burn-rate and user-impact alerts, then moves non-urgent signals into dashboards or review workflows.

faq.question: Is it suitable for regulated services?
faq.answer: Yes, as planning guidance. Review targets, dashboards, and data handling with your compliance and security teams.
